title: Per-batch runtime-aware quant eval with semantic-drift scoring
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build an eval harness and gating logic that measures the quality impact of int8/int4 (AWQ and GPTQ) quant profiles across production-like runtime conditions (batch sizes, sequence length distributions, KV-cache warm states) and compute a semantic-drift score that can be used to auto-tune deployment thresholds and rollout gates.

Motivation: Existing quant impact tests run static prompt sets at a single concurrency/sequence length. In production, cost/latency decisions depend strongly on batching, prefix reuse, and cold vs warmed KV cache. We need a single signal (semantic-drift) that combines embedding-distance drift, rollout-sensitive regression counts, and weighted user-facing metrics to drive automatic threshold tuning and safe rollouts.

High-level approach:
1) Create a per-batch simulator that replays sampled production traces (batch sizes, seq lengths, cache hit rates) against model variants: fp16 baseline, AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4.
2) For each request, compute: (a) token-level generation deltas (logit/entropy differences), (b) semantic embeddings for outputs (client embedding model) and compute cosine drift relative to baseline, (c) semantic similarity-based signal mapped to an interpretable drift score.
3) Cohort-weighted aggregation: weight drift by customer cohorts and route-level SLA sensitivity (low-latency routes get stricter weight).
4) Generate multi-dimensional curves: drift vs P95 latency, drift vs per-token cost, drift vs cache-hit-rate.
5) Auto-threshold tuner: use the curves to suggest threshold breakpoints. The tuner proposes rollback and canary window sizes for progressive rollouts.
6) Integrate with Console: surface per-route drift, recommended guardrail thresholds, and a suggested quant profile.

Deliverables:
- A reproducible harness (k8s job + ephemeral dataset) that can run a sweep across quant profiles and runtime settings.
- A semantic-drift scorer (deterministic pipeline) with configurable thresholds and cohort weights.
- A visualization dashboard (Grafana) showing heatmaps and tradeoff curves.
- An auto-threshold recommender that outputs YAML for rollout policies (canary_pct, rollback_condition, drift_threshold).
tasks: Design per-batch runtime replay harness (Marcus) - include seq length distribution generator and KV-cache warm/cold modes
Implement model runner wrappers for AWQ and GPTQ profiles (engine infra) - re-use runtime-1.18 kernels when possible
Embed-output pipeline: choose embedding model, compute cosine distances, normalize to drift score (Sofia)
Cohort weighting logic: map customer routes to sensitivity classes and apply weights
Auto-threshold tuner: prototype greedy and simulated-annealing approaches for breakpoint selection
Grafana panels: heatmap (drift x latency x cost), per-route threshold recommendations
Integration: output threshold YAML and test in canary rollout flow with console-2026.03 feature flag
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run end-to-end with baseline and 4 quant profiles on a sampled production trace within a single k8s job
Semantic-drift score correlates with human-evaluated regressions on a 200-sample manual set (pearson r >= 0.65)
Auto-threshold recommender produces threshold suggestions that, when applied in a staged canary, prevent >90% of observed manual regressions during a simulated 1000-request replay
Dashboard shows per-route drift and latency/cost tradeoffs and is accessible via a Grafana link
Documentation and runbook added (how to interpret drift, when to accept quant recommendations)
